messages:
sara: FYI - after the dedicated deploy at 03:00 we ran the deploy-time warmers and saw overall KV prefix hit-rate collapse from ~48% -> ~12% within ~10m. attaching quick logs. :confused:

matt: ouch. do we have a timeline? was this only on one pool or across all zones?

sara: across the LA pool and one AZ in eu-west. timeline: warmer jobs started at 03:02, autoscaler triggered scale-down at 03:06, scale-up at 03:08, hit-rate stayed low after scale-up.

juan: i pulled the profiler traces. two suspicious things: 1) the warmers were sending highly fragmented batches (lots of size-1) so batching heuristics didn't merge prefixes; 2) the warmer harness was generating random prefix tails for 'diversity' which prevented reuse of cached KV entries.

lee: thanks. i also checked the runtime kernel selection logs — during the period we fell back to the small-seq kernel (seq_len heuristic kicked in) which is slightly slower and has a different KV cache key path in the code. not sure if that caused key mismatch, but it changes the prefill ordering.

matt: do you have the exact log lines?

lee: paste below (cleaned):
```
[2026-04-12T03:06:12Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=small_seq_opt reason=avg_seq_len<=64
[2026-04-12T03:06:12Z] kv_cache: prefill_order=interleaved ttl=300s
[2026-04-12T03:06:15Z] batcher: emitted_batch_size=1
```

juan: here's the warmer config we accidentally shipped:
```
warmer_config:
  parallel_jobs: 60
  prefixes_per_job: 300
  randomize_tail: true   # <--- this is the problem
  sampling_source: live-samples
  target_pool: dedicated-la
```

juan: randomize_tail=true means we append a random token sequence to each prefix sample, so KV keys never match between requests. on top of that the batcher emits single-request batches for many of these, so there's no prefix sharing at runtime.

sara: that explains the 48->12 drop. profiler stats i collected: prefill_hit_rate: 0.48 -> 0.12, prefill_miss_cost_avg_tokens: 42, p50_latency_ms: 26, p95_latency_ms: 218 (spike during scale events).

matt: nice catch. so root cause = faulty warmer config + autoscaler timing that evicted warm caches?

lee: autoscaler contributed: scale-down reduces total cache cardinality (evictions), then new nodes get traffic but with randomized tails so misses can't rebuild hot prefixes. also the small_seq kernel switch changed prefill ordering so even identical prefixes end up prefilled in different slots for a few seconds which hurts immediate reuse.

juan: proposed fixes:
- patch warmer harness: set randomize_tail=false and use sampled canonical tails (from top-100 prefixes)
- bump warmer_jobs splay so we don't flood the pool exactly at deploy time (stagger across 10m)
- change warmer to submit batched grouped-by-prefix requests (hint: group by prefix hash before sending)

sara: +1. also add a short-term mitigation: when autoscaler scales up within X minutes of a deploy, trigger a targeted prefill pass for top-500 prefixes rather than running the full synthetic job.

matt: can we add an assertion to CI so warmer_config.randomize_tail cannot be true for deploy-time jobs?

juan: yes i can add a linter that rejects deploy-time warmer configs with randomize_tail or with prefixes_per_job > 1000.

lee: i'll follow up on the kernel selector: make prefill_order deterministic across kernel choices (i'll open PR with a fallback deterministic ordering). that should reduce the transient mismatch window.

sara: quick action items:
- juan: change warmer binary to randomize_tail=false, group-by-prefix, stagger schedule (ETA today EOD)
- matt: add CI linter (ETA tomorrow)
- lee: PR for deterministic prefill order (ETA 2 days)
- ops: run targeted top-500 prefill for LA pool after patch (manual)

deploy-bot: deploy started: warmer-patch-v1 -> staging at 12:04 UTC :rocket:

matt: once the patch is canaried, run the same perf job to verify hit-rate recovery. expecting >40% baseline.

juan: test run locally w/ fixed config: prefill_hit_rate ~43% after 8m. sharing script in #devex. :thumbsup:

sara: great work team. let's keep an eye on p95s during the next autoscale flurry.

lee: noted — i'll add a lightweight metric alert for prefill_order-jitter and kernel-switch-count so we can catch this earlier.

matt: thanks all. followups in PRs. :slightly_smiling_face:
